case_name: Kaithakulangara Kunhikannan vs Nellatham Veettil Malu
facts_of_case: Petitioner, a Hindu husband, sought judicial separation from his wife under Section 10 of the Hindu Marriage Act. The trial court granted judicial separation and ordered maintenance to the respondent at Rs. 25/- per mensem.

legal_principles.principle: A wife who has been living in adultery is not entitled to maintenance under Section 25 of the Hindu Marriage Act, unless there are very special grounds.
legal_principles.held: In our opinion, such a meeting place of law and morality is Section 25 of the Hindu Marriage Act, or for the matter of that Section 18 of the Hindu Adoption and Maintenance Act. In the exercise of judicial discretion, expressly vested in Courts of Law under Section 25 (1) of the Hindu Marriage Act, a Judge should, unless there be very special grounds, leave a wife divorced on the ground of proved unchastity or adultery, to the resources of her immorality and deny her the lawful means of support, by passing a decree for maintenance in her favour.
cited_cases: Sachindra Nath v. Banamala, AIR 1960 Cal 575
Amar Kanta v. Soyana, AIR 1960 Cal 438

legal_principles.principle: A finding of unchastity recorded during judicial separation proceedings regarding the wife's unchastity must and should be taken into account when an order is being passed under Section 25 (1) of the Hindu Marriage Act.
legal_principles.held: In my opinion, if a subsequent conduct of the wife who has become unchaste can form the basis for cancellation of an order passed under Setton 25 (1), a finding recorded during the judicial separation proceedings regarding the unchastity of the wife must and should be taken into account even in the first instance, when an order is being passed under Section 25 (1) of the Act.
cited_cases: Vaidialingam, J. posed the question in the following manner: 'Where a charge of adultery is the very foundation of a claim for asking judicial separation and that claim is accepted by a court notwithstanding that finding the respondent against whom that finding has been entered, can claim, as of right, to be awarded maintenance under Section 25 of the Act'
use_in: cases involving judicial separation and adultery

outcome.final_order: The final order was that the respondent is entitled only to bare maintenance allowance, payable monthly from the date of the order.

use_for_drafting: drafting a petition for judicial separation under Section 10 of the Hindu Marriage Act
advising on maintenance rights in cases of adultery
assisting with divorce proceedings in Kerala
